prayerExcerpt.en-US: "He that humbleth himself shall be exalted."

meta.face: A Breton Gallo-Roman of about eighty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a pale, soft, pink complexion and a PEAR-SHAPED face — NARROW temples and a narrowish, high, lined forehead widening down to FULL, soft, heavy JOWLS and a broad, soft double chin; a LONG, THICK, straight nose with a rounded tip; small, gentle, deep-set brown eyes with heavy pouches beneath, lowered in humility; sparse, faint white brows; a small mouth with a soft, full lower lip; a thin ring of white hair round a bald crown; the gaze modest and kind, down toward the child.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; the book's engraving shows a mitred bishop giving alms at a church door among the poor and crippled, and the card keeps the alms. His Breton birth, abbacy and see are from the book and Wikipedia; Angers stands on the Maine (Wikipedia). The clean-shaven pear-shaped old face is our choice, to set him apart from St. David on the same day.
